clips.send: A guy sends this to his gym buddy who drinks soy protein shakes daily - anxiety about what's actually in his food.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says soy and high-fructose corn syrup are in nearly every processed food today, and both are tied to lower testosterone.

His reasoning: soy contains plant compounds that mimic estrogen, and a lot of corn syrup traces back to corn bred to fatten livestock fast.

Kevin Trudeau's take: that's part of why so many people feel tired with no drive, even when nothing else in their life changed.

Worth a look next time you check a label: how far down the ingredient list is soy or corn syrup?

What ingredient surprised you the first time you actually found it on a label?

#kevintrudeau #soy #cornsyrup #hormonehealth #readthelabel #questioneverything

clips.send: Someone who's tried to quit smoking five times sends this to a friend doing the same - anger at being programmed without knowing it.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says the hardest part about quitting cigarettes isn't the chemical - it's the programming.

His point: nicotine withdrawal is mostly over within 24 hours. What keeps people smoking after that is psychological, built by decades of advertising linking cigarettes to coolness and rebellion, right down to the old movie scene of a cigarette as a man's last request.

Kevin Trudeau's take: once you see where that pull actually came from, it loses some of its grip.

The same kind of programming shows up in food ads too.

What's a craving you traced back to an old ad once you really looked at it?

#kevintrudeau #addiction #bigtobacco #psychology #quitsmoking #questioneverything
